user: I'm CUS-0004. Transaction TX-0401, 240.00 EUR: the goods never arrived. Which reason code applies?
answer:
Your account is confirmed as CUS-0004 (Danylo Kovalenko), on account ACC-1005.

For a payment where the goods never arrived, the applicable reason code is **goods_not_received**. The `service_not_rendered` code is for services that were paid for but not delivered.

Under Verta's dispute rules, goods_not_received has a 90-day window counted from the transaction date. I haven't checked TX-0401 yet, so I can't confirm it is still within that window. If you'd like to proceed, I can run the eligibility check on TX-0401 under this reason code. If it is eligible, I can then open the dispute for the 240.00 EUR amount. Would you like me to do that?

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Notifications
## Dispute updates
A dispute generates a notification on every state change. The notification
names the state, never the internal reason for a decision.
